Surah 84: Al-Inshiqaq (The Splitting Asunder)

Makkan, and its verses are twenty-five.

﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾, i.e., with the clouds, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the day the sky will split open with clouds﴾. And it is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that it splits from the Milky Way (al-Majarra).

﴿And it has listened to its Lord﴾: that is, it has complied (وَاسْتَمَعَتْ) and submitted (انْقادَتْ وأذْعَنَتْ) to the effect of His power, may He be exalted, when His will became attached to its splitting. It complies as an obedient subordinate complies when the command of a commander who is obeyed reaches him. The mention of the title "Lord" (al-rububiyyah, lordship) together with the pronoun referring to it indicates the cause of the ruling. This clause and its counterpart that follows are, in the sense of informing, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We came willingly﴾ (41:11). They show that what is attributed to the heaven and the earth, such as splitting, stretching and other things, proceeds in accordance with wisdom (al-hikmah), as has been pointed out earlier.

﴿And it is right that it should﴾: that is, it is made deserving (حَقِيقَةٌ) of listening and compliance. But this is not after it was not so; rather, it is so in itself and in its very essence, from the expression "he is entitled to such-and-such" (مَحْقُوقٌ بِكَذا) and "he is worthy of it" (حَقِيقٌ بِهِ). The meaning is: it complied with its Lord while being worthy of that. However, this does not mean that the intended meaning is the particularity of its own essence among all other things that are subject to power. Rather, it is the particularity of the overpowering divine power, by which every possible thing is accomplished and from which none of the matters can escape. Therefore, the proper analysis of the clause is that it is an interjected clause (اعْتِراضًا) that confirms what precedes it, not a clause conjoined to it (مَعْطُوفَةً عَلَيْهِ).

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, i.e., spread flat by the removal of its mountains and hills from their places and by leveling it, so that it becomes a smooth plain (qā'an ṣafṣafan), in which you see no crookedness (ʿiwajan) or unevenness (amtan). Or it is increased in extent and expanse, from madda-hu in the sense of amadda-hu, i.e., he increased it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 4:

﴿And it casts out what is within it﴾. That is: it throws out what is in its belly of the dead and the treasures, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾.

﴿And empties itself﴾: and it empties itself of what is within it to the utmost degree of emptiness, until nothing of it remains within it, as though it had exerted its utmost effort in that.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 5:**

﴿And it has listened to its Lord and it was bound to do so﴾ in casting out and emptying itself.

﴿And it is bound (ḥuqqat)﴾, i.e., it is fitting for it to do so, meaning that its condition in relation to the Lordly power is that (p-132) ... [text continues]

The repetition of the word "idhā" (when), along with the unity of the actions attributed to the heaven and the earth occurring within the extended time that it denotes, has had its secret explained previously.

O human being, you are laboring toward your Lord with great toil, and you will meet Him.

Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 6:

﴿O humankind, indeed you are toiling toward your Lord with arduous toil, and you will meet Him.﴾ That is: striving and exerting yourself toward death and what follows it of the states that are described by "meeting" (al-liqa'), exerting yourself greatly in that. For al-kadh (toil) is the striving of the self in work and the exertion in it, to the extent that it leaves its mark upon it, from kadaha jildahu (he scratched his skin) when he scratched it.

﴿Then you will meet Him﴾: that is, you will meet Him after that without doubt, with nothing to turn you away from Him. His exalted saying:

*

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verses 7–8:

﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾ ...etc. It is said: the answer to "idha" (when) is as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then, if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O man﴾ ...etc. is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad). It is also said that the answer is omitted, for the sake of awe and to indicate that expression falls short of explaining it, or for reliance upon what has passed in Surat al-Takwir and al-Infitar. It is also said that the answer is what is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O man﴾ ...etc., its estimate being: "Man will meet his toil." It is also said that the answer is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then you will meet it﴾, and what precedes it is a parenthetical clause. It is also said that the answer is ﴿O man﴾ ...etc., with the verb "say" (qawl) understood, meaning: "[It will be said:] an easy, simple reckoning, with no questioning or objection." It is reported from al-Siddiqa (may Allah be pleased with her) that it means that he is made to recognize his sins and then they are overlooked for him.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verses 7–8:

﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾ ...etc. It is said: the answer to "idha" (when) is as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then, if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O man﴾ ...etc. is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad). It is also said that the answer is omitted, for the sake of awe and to indicate that expression falls short of explaining it, or for reliance upon what has passed in Surat al-Takwir and al-Infitar. It is also said that the answer is what is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O man﴾ ...etc., its estimate being: "Man will meet his toil." It is also said that the answer is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then you will meet it﴾, and what precedes it is a parenthetical clause. It is also said that the answer is ﴿O man﴾ ...etc., with the verb "say" (qawl) understood, meaning: "[It will be said:] an easy, simple reckoning, with no questioning or objection." ﴿And he returns to his people, joyful.﴾ That is, to his kinsfolk among the believers, or to the company of believers, delighted with his state, saying: "Here, read my book!" It has also been said: "to his people in Paradise," meaning the maidens of paradise (ḥūr) and the youths (ghilmān).

﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾: that is, he is given it with his left hand from behind his back. It is said: his right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand is placed behind his back, so he is given his record with his left hand. And it is said: his left hand is wrenched out from behind his back.

﴿So he will call for destruction (thubur)﴾. That is: he will wish for destruction, and thubur is ruin/perdition; he will call out, "Alas, my destruction! Come, for this is your time," and how could that be for him?

﴿And he will burn in a blazing fire﴾ means: he will enter it. It is read "yaṣlā" (with the first letter open, yaṣlā), as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿and the burning of Hellfire﴾, and it is read "wa-yuṣlā" (with a damma on the yā’), as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿and We will cast him into Hell﴾.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 13:

﴿Indeed, he was among his family﴾ — that is, among his household and his kin in the worldly life.

﴿Joyful﴾ (p-133) — pampered, insolent, exultant, rejoicing, in the manner of the habit of the wicked (fujjar), who are not concerned by it and for whom the matters of the Hereafter do not occur to their minds, and who do not reflect upon the outcomes; and he was not ﴿sorrowful﴾, reflecting on his state and his final destiny, as is the custom of the righteous (sulaha') and the God-fearing (muttaqun). The sentence is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) explaining the cause of what precedes it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return﴾ is a reason for his joy in the worldly life; that is, he thought that he would never return to God, Exalted is He, denying the Resurrection. And "in" (إنْ) is a lightened form of "anna" (أنّ), which together with what follows it fills the place of the two objects of "thought" (ظنّ), or one of them, according to the well-known difference of opinion.

Yes indeed. ﴿Yes﴾ is an affirmation of what follows "never" (lan). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾ confirms and gives the reason for it. That is: Yes, he will certainly return (to life), for indeed his Lord, who created him, was Seeing of him and of his deeds that necessitate recompense, such that nothing of them is hidden, so there must be his return, his reckoning, and his recompense for them, without doubt.

It was also said: the two verses were revealed concerning Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad and his brother al-Aswad.

Verse 84:16: ﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾. It is the redness that is seen on the horizon of the west after sunset, or the whiteness that follows it. It was named so for its thinness (ruqqah), and from the same root is "shafaqah" (compassion), which is an expression for the tenderness of the heart.

And by the night and what it gathers together (﴿واللَّيْلِ وما وسَقَ﴾). "Wasaqa" means to gather and collect together; it is said: "wasaqahu fa-ittasaqa" and "istawsaqa," meaning he gathered it and it became gathered. "Ma" here is an expression for that which gathers during the night and returns to its place, of beasts and other things.
﴿By the moon when it becomes full﴾. That is: it gathers and becomes full as a full moon on the fourteenth night.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 19:

﴿You shall surely encounter stage after stage﴾ That is: you shall surely encounter state after state, each one matching its fellow in severity and awfulness. It has also been said: "ṭabaq" is the plural of "ṭabaqah," which means rank or level, and this is the more fitting reading for "rakb" (riding/mounting), which indicates ascending. The meaning then is: you shall ride through states after states, which are levels in severity, some higher than others, namely death and what follows it of the stations of the Resurrection and its calamities.

It was also recited as "latarkabanna" in the singular, addressing man according to the wording rather than according to his encompassing all its individuals, as in the first reading. It was recited with a kasra on the ba' as an address to the soul (nafs), and as "liyarkabanna" with the ya', meaning: man shall ride. The position of "ʿan ṭabaq" is in the accusative, being either an adjective of "ṭabaqan," meaning: a level passing beyond another level; or a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "latarkabanna," meaning: passing beyond, or passing beyond one another, according to the reading.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 20:

The fa' (the particle of consequence) in His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ serves to link what follows it, namely the denunciation and wonder, to what precedes it of the states of the Resurrection and its terrors, which necessitate belief and prostration. That is: if their condition on the Day of Resurrection is as has been mentioned, then what is it with them, while they are not believing? That is, what prevents them from belief, when its requirements are mutually reinforcing?

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 21:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾ is a conditional clause (jumlah shartiyyah) whose place in the i'rab is accusative as a circumstantial clause (haliyyah), coordinated with what precedes it. That is: what prevents them from prostrating, and from humbling themselves and submitting when the Qur'an is recited?

It was said: one day the Prophet (ﷺ) recited "Prostrate and draw near" (surah 96), so he prostrated, and those believers with him prostrated, while the Quraysh were clapping above their heads and whistling, and this verse was revealed. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, used this as evidence for the obligation of the prostration (sajdah).

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that there is no prostration in al-Mufassal (the later short surahs of the Qur'an).

It is reported from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he prostrated during it and said: "By Allah, I did not prostrate except after I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

It is reported from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: "I prayed behind Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them, and they prostrated."

It is reported from al-Hasan: it is not obligatory.

Translation:

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny it (the Qur'an)﴾, the Qur'an which speaks of what has been mentioned of the conditions of the Resurrection and its terrors, even though the grounds that necessitate its affirmation are established; and for this reason they do not humble themselves when it is recited.

God knows best what they conceal (﴿وما يوعون﴾ = what they store up). That is, what they hide and gather in their hearts and breasts of disbelief, envy, transgression and hatred; or, what they gather in their records of evil deeds and store up for themselves of the various kinds of punishment, [this being] a knowledge that is practical (ʿilman filiyyan).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 24:

﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ Because His knowledge, exalted is He, of that in the manner mentioned necessitates their punishment inevitably.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 84, verse 25:

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ — this is an disconnected exception (istithna' munqati') if the relative pronoun is taken to refer to all believers in general, and a connected exception (istithna' muttasil) if it is meant to refer to those among them who believe after that. And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿For them is a reward never to be cut off﴾ — i.e., unceasing, or "bestowed upon them as a favor" — is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf) that confirms what the exception implies regarding the removal of punishment from them, and explains its manner and its being accompanied by the great reward.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Inshiqaq, Allah will protect him from being given his record behind his back."
